summary: Post-market, 2026-10-08: the composite rose 1.35 to 50.84 and stays in the caution band, with the goldilocks regime intact and model confidence at 0.9066. The US session was a broad de-rating of the AI complex rather than a macro shock: the Nasdaq fell 1.25%, the S&P 500 fell 0.47% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.39%, while the Dow rose 0.1%, after OpenAI told investors it had reached roughly $50B of annualized revenue. NVIDIA closed at -2.9435, Broadcom at -4.3478, Micron at -4.7941, AMD at -3.8987 and Tesla at -0.7438, and 18 of the 22 sectors and themes in the layer fell, led by quantum computing at -4.2547, memory at -4.082 and networking at -4.0299, against AI software at 0.8584 and digital advertising at 0.724. Cross-asset confirmation rose to 0.875, with 7 of the 8 production signals triggered and the largest single contribution at 7.5. The newest rates observation edged up, the 10-year to 5.28 from 5.27 and the real rate to 2.92 from 2.91, while the 2-year fell to 4.77 from 4.79 and the 10Y/2Y curve widened to 0.51; credit split, HY OAS widening to 3.09 from 3.03 and IG OAS tightening to 0.82 from 0.83; VIX at 15.08 from 15.01 stayed at the 23.57th percentile. Mainland China's first session after the 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-07 holiday also sold off, 688825.SH at -7.7934, 300223.SZ at -7.2861 and 603986.SH at -5.51.

top_risk_drivers.claim: AI-linked equities sank after OpenAI disclosed roughly $50B of annualized revenue: NVIDIA closed at -2.9435, Broadcom at -4.3478, Micron at -4.7941, AMD at -3.8987 and Tesla at -0.7438.

The damage concentrated in AI hardware rather than the whole market: quantum computing at -4.2547, memory at -4.082, networking at -4.0299 and semiconductor equipment at -2.7744, with 18 of the 22 sectors and themes in the layer lower.

The macro leg remains the highest-scoring dimension at 71.16: the 10-year real rate at 2.92 and the 10-year yield at 5.28 both sit at the 99.84th percentile, and the newest observation edged up rather than eased.

Cross-asset confirmation supplies the largest single contribution at 7.5 on a reading of 0.875, with 7 of the 8 production signals triggered: the dollar at 121.3848, the real rate at 2.92, small caps lagging by -8.7223, bitcoin and copper lower and gold higher.
Equity structure deteriorated further: new lows outnumber new highs 18 to 3 of 156 names, with breadth at 0.5742 of 155 names above their 200-day average.

supporting_signals.claim: Mainland China's first session after the 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-07 holiday confirmed the same complex: 10 of the 11 names in the layer fell, 688825.SH at -7.7934, 300223.SZ at -7.2861, 603986.SH at -5.51 and 301308.SZ at -4.4149, with only 000021.SZ higher at 0.8833.
Crypto de-rated harder than the equity tape: bitcoin fell 2.11684% to 81722, ether fell 4.22517% to 2466.17 and solana fell 5.97733% to 109.25.
Small caps and semis lag badly on a relative basis: small caps by -8.7223 and semis by -5.626.
Liquidity tightened on a same-day vintage: reverse repo fell to 0.335 from 2.338, the fifth-largest driver contribution at 3.814.

contradicting_signals.claim: Credit gave a split read rather than a stressed one: HY OAS widened to 3.09 from 3.03 while IG OAS tightened to 0.82 from 0.83, and the high-yield leg was the only one of the 8 production signals not to trigger.
Volatility did not confirm the de-rating: VIX at 15.08 from 15.01 is only at the 23.57th percentile, and its 2026-10-07 vintage is aligned with the rates leg rather than frozen.

The dollar input behind the largest single driver has not advanced: it stands at 121.3848 from 121.7882 on a 2026-10-02 vintage, unchanged across 3 consecutive runs, so the cross-asset reading rests partly on a stale leg.
Policy pricing runs against the rates move: Fedwatch implies 4.065 against a delivered rate of 3.88, a hike, while the 2-year fell to 4.77 from 4.79 and the 10Y/2Y curve widened to 0.51.
The de-rating was rotational rather than a uniform exit: AI software rose 0.8584 and digital advertising 0.724, and the Dow closed up 0.1% while the Nasdaq fell 1.25%.
